# dockercompose_project (Resource)

A Docker Compose project, deployed like `docker compose up -d`.

Changes are applied in place: compose recreates only the services whose configuration changed. On every refresh the provider checks that each service has a running container (or, for one-shot services, one that exited successfully) and that the mirrored files are unchanged. Any difference shows up in the next plan.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "random_password" "db" {
  length = 32
}

# Compose content as native HCL. Outputs of other resources can be used
# directly, including values only known during apply.
resource "dockercompose_project" "app" {
  name = "app"

  compose = yamlencode({
    services = {
      db = {
        image   = "postgres:17-alpine"
        restart = "unless-stopped"
        environment = {
          POSTGRES_PASSWORD = "$${DB_PASSWORD}"
        }
        volumes = ["./data:/var/lib/postgresql/data"]
      }
    }
  })

  env = {
    DB_PASSWORD = random_password.db.result
  }
}

# An existing compose file works too.
resource "dockercompose_project" "proxy" {
  name    = "proxy"
  compose = file("${path.module}/proxy/compose.yaml")
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `compose` (String) Compose file content. Use `file()`, `templatefile()` or `yamlencode({...})`. Relative paths resolve against `project_dir` on the Docker host. `${VAR}` references are interpolated from `env`, never from the environment of the machine running Terraform.
- `name` (String) Compose project name. Changing it replaces the project.

### Optional

- `env` (Map of String, Sensitive) Interpolation variables, the equivalent of a `.env` file. Stored in state and written to `project_dir/.env` with mode `0600`.
- `profiles` (List of String) Compose profiles to enable.
- `project_dir` (String) Absolute project directory on the Docker host. Defaults to `/opt/dockercompose/<name>`. The compose file and `.env` are mirrored here when `write_files` is set, so `docker compose` works on the host.
- `remove_orphans` (Boolean) Remove containers of services no longer in the compose file. Defaults to `true`.
- `remove_volumes_on_destroy` (Boolean) Also remove named volumes when the project is destroyed. Defaults to `false`.
- `wait` (Boolean) Wait until services are running or healthy, like `docker compose up --wait`. Defaults to `true`.
- `wait_timeout` (String) Maximum time to wait, as a Go duration such as `90s` or `5m`. Defaults to `5m`.
- `write_files` (Boolean) Mirror `compose.yaml` and `.env` into `project_dir`. Defaults to `true`.

### Read-Only

- `config_hash` (String) Hash of the inputs that define the deployment. After a refresh that found drift, it starts with `drifted:` and names the differences.
- `id` (String) The project name.
- `services` (Map of String) State of each service's containers, for example `running` or `exited (0)`.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Import by compose project name. The project must have been deployed by this
# provider with write_files enabled, because compose and env are read back from
# the files mirrored into its project directory.
terraform import dockercompose_project.app app
```
